A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the statement 'every full subcategory of a (dual of a) locally presentable category which is limit-closed and closed under some of the basic operations is orthogonal' is equivalent to a large cardinal principle.
the statement 'every full subcategory of a category is orthogonal' is undecidable for categories of small dimensions, while for large dimensions it is decidable and equivalent to a large cardinal.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of a 'locally presentable' category is not a good analogue of the notion of a Grothendieck topos.
